evidence.claim: DOE said Centrus produced the first amounts of HALEU under the DOE HALEU Demonstration project at Piketon, Ohio, using 16 advanced centrifuges.

memory_update.text: LEU should remain the primary US-listed underfollowed candidate for direct HALEU enrichment exposure; survival depends on evidence of scalable commercial enrichment economics beyond DOE demonstration/initial contracts.

BWXT is a larger reference candidate but important for the fuel-fabrication/downblending/qualified-manufacturing side of the HALEU chokepoint; track whether advanced-fuel work becomes financially material.
ASPI is a speculative-shadow HALEU entrant; include only with explicit licensing, technology-validation, financing, and binding-customer verification gates.
LTBR is a speculative-shadow fuel-design candidate; relevance depends on HALEU availability plus fuel testing, licensing, fabrication, and customer adoption milestones.

node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication, and fuel security
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow US-listed universe tied directly to the nuclear fuel-cycle bottleneck. The strongest direct public-market exposure is Centrus Energy for US HALEU enrichment, with BWX Technologies as a larger reference name for HALEU processing, downblending, TRISO and specialty fuel fabrication. The underfollowed/speculative lane includes ASP Isotopes, which is attempting HALEU enrichment through Quantum Leap Energy/Necsa, and Lightbridge, an advanced fuel design company whose relevance depends on HALEU availability and successful fuel qualification. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation.
